one_line_contribution: A controlled dissociation test showing that what transfers across domains in reflective prompt optimization is the optimizer's harvested failure-symptom-to-edit knowledge injected into GEPA's reflection step, not the optimized prompt skeleton, evaluated as a Pareto sample-efficiency curve with a measured crossover budget rather than a leaderboard win.
closest_prior_work: Two clusters, only one of which the proposal engages. (a) REMO, which the proposal itself cites and correctly characterizes as a within-domain single-benchmark mistake notebook — the proposal's delta over it is cross-domain evaluation plus controls, i.e. an evaluation contribution, not a mechanism. (b) The cluster the proposal never mentions: ExpeL-style cross-task natural-language insight extraction from past success/failure pools (already claims transfer to unseen tasks), Dynamic Cheatsheet-style test-time strategy memory, and above all the 2025 agentic-context-engineering line that builds an incrementally curated 'playbook' of strategy bullets via a generator/reflector/curator loop and benchmarks it directly against GEPA. That last one uses the same word for the same object and already reports beating GEPA; the defensible difference here is that its playbook conditions the executor on domain-specific context whereas this one conditions the meta-level reflector on domain-scrubbed rules — a real but narrow distinction that the proposal has not articulated because it does not cite the work. A reviewer who knows that literature will read this as ExpeL/REMO lifted one level up the stack onto GEPA, which is exactly the 'domain swap' the track brief warns scores as a modest delta.
strongest_objection: The design cannot support the two claims it advertises as central, and this is visible from its own numbers. The Measurement section states per-run test SD ~3 points and n=30 paired observations detecting a 1.5-point mean paired difference at 80% power. The headline prediction then asserts (i) convergence to cold-start by 300 rollouts with a gap <=1.5 points, and (ii) 'playbook transfer is never worse than cold-start by more than the noise floor on any target'. Both are equivalence claims. (i) sits exactly at the MDE, so the study cannot distinguish 'converged' from 'still ahead by 1.4' or 'behind by 1.4' — the Pareto shape, which is the paper's whole framing, is asserted at the resolution limit of the instrument. (ii) is a per-target claim resting on 5 seeds each; with 6 targets and SD 3, at least one target showing a spurious 2-4 point deficit is the expected outcome, so the pre-registered refutation condition will most likely fire for reasons unrelated to the hypothesis and will have to be rescued post hoc. Compounding this, the prediction promises a crossover-budget bootstrap CI 'narrower than the checkpoint spacing' for a predicted crossover of 120-250 rollouts when the bracketing checkpoints are 100/200/300 — a crossover of two noisy monotone curves estimated from five discrete points with SD 3 will not yield an interval that tight, and claiming it in advance suggests the interval width was written as an aspiration rather than derived. This reproduces failure mode 2 from the track brief in a proposal that explicitly set out to avoid it.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes. (1) Replace the equivalence assertions with a TOST-style pre-registered equivalence margin and power the 300-rollout convergence test and the per-target no-harm test for that margin — which will require more seeds per target (10-15) or fewer arms, and should be traded against the ablation list rather than added to it. (2) Pre-register the source-target distance partition before running: the current target set includes HotpotQA against a 2WikiMultiHop source and BBH-against-BBH-other-clusters, which are near-in-domain pairs that dilute the average and, worse, blunt the dissociation claim because the skeleton baseline should also succeed on them; report distant pairs as the primary analysis and near pairs separately. (3) Fix the compute arithmetic or cut the grid, and state the amortization argument explicitly: the playbook costs 6 sources x 300 rollouts x 3 seeds = 5,400 harvest rollouts, so give the break-even number of target tasks at which the transferred playbook is cheaper than cold-start, otherwise the sample-efficiency claim is only true after an unstated fixed cost. (4) Add a genuinely off-domain token-matched null (rules harvested for some unrelated skill) alongside the anti-matched shuffle, because with only 20-60 rules an anti-matched top-3 still returns on-topic prompt-optimization advice, so the shuffle control is likely to null out for the wrong reason and kill a live hypothesis.
missing_baseline: A within-run self-harvested playbook: run cold-start GEPA on the target task and accumulate the same SYMPTOM/EDIT rules from that run's own early failures and validated edit deltas, injected into its own later reflection calls, at matched rollouts and matched reflection tokens. This is the cheap competitor a practitioner would actually reach for, it requires no source harvesting at all, and if it matches cross-domain transfer then the entire harvesting apparatus and the transfer framing contribute nothing. The proposal's controls are all aimed at the wrong alternative: baseline (iv), the hand-written human checklist, tests whether the rules are generic, and the shuffled ablation tests whether content matters, but neither tests whether the knowledge needed to be imported from other domains rather than generated on the spot. A second cheap omission: a zero-rollout playbook generated by asking the same frontier reflection model to write 40 SYMPTOM/EDIT rules cold, formatted identically — a stronger and less sandbaggable version of the hand-written checklist. I would also expect a reviewer to demand plain best-of-N prompt sampling at matched rollouts, which is often competitive with reflective search at the 25-50 rollout budgets where this paper claims its win.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty. Judged on what the text actually provides, the Related Work section shows partial recency awareness — REMO is dated 2025 and a cross-tier transfer paper is dated 2026 — but it reports no searches, names no search scope or date window, and conspicuously omits the recent preprint line most likely to scoop it: 2025 agentic-context-engineering work that incrementally curates a reusable strategy 'playbook' through a reflector/curator loop and benchmarks it head-to-head against GEPA, plus ExpeL-style cross-task insight pools and Dynamic Cheatsheet-style test-time strategy memory. In a subfield where the threatening artifact is a three-month-old arXiv posting, an unsearched novelty claim over a neighborhood the track brief already flagged as crowded is a substantive weakness, not a neutral omission, and it is the main reason novelty is scored at 5 rather than 6-7 despite the genuinely good control set. The proposal must state which recent preprints it checked and articulate the meta-level (optimizer-conditioning) versus object-level (executor-conditioning) distinction explicitly, because that distinction is currently its only defensible novelty and it is not made anywhere in the text.
